content:
priya: Nightly concurrency sweep CI is flaky again — p95 spikes randomly on the 2k token workload.
priya: Example failure from last night: runner finished but latency jump at concurrency=48.
priya: logs:
```
[2026-03-18 03:12:45] run_id=nightly-2026-03-18-2k conv=48 tokens/sec=210 p50=18ms p95=1.2s p99=2.3s
[2026-03-18 03:12:46] WARN kv-cache miss rate increased to 14%
[2026-03-18 03:12:46] WARN shard_rebalance triggered, detaching worker-7
[2026-03-18 03:12:46] ERROR observed latency regression vs baseline: +760ms (baseline p95=460ms)
```
priya: It looks like shard rebalance coincides with the spike. The runner's rebalancer might be too aggressive under the concurrency sweep.
matt: Thanks — I saw similar from the weekend sweep. Could be the auto-shard policy reacting to transient queue length.
matt: Can you paste the runner config used by the CI job?
priya: config snippet from ci job:
```
runner: {
  worker_count: 12,
  max_batch_tokens: 4096,
  auto_shard: true,
  shard_rebalance_threshold: 0.25,
  kv_cache_enabled: true,
  cpu_backoff_ms: 40
}
```
ana: (typo) ana: I think 12 workers + concurrency=48 means each worker gets 4 concurrent streams; rebalance threshold 0.25 might cause churn when one batch is slow.
david: Also the CI harness currently treats any p95 > baseline*1.3 as fail, but we don't account for GPU warmup or first-epoch jitters. CI should ignore the first 2 minutes of a run.
priya: Good call. Currently runner-runner.sh does not exclude warmup. Here is the CI command used:
```
./eval-runner --profile performance --duration 300 --concurrency 48 --token-limit 2000 --report /tmp/report.json
```
ci-bot: @priya created issue #412: "Nightly concurrency sweep: shard rebalance causes intermittent p95 spikes"
priya: Proposal: for nightly sweep tests, set auto_shard=false and add a 60s warmup window that is excluded from metrics. Also record GPU util and oss_latency breakdown in the report.
matt: Agreed. Also add metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, gpu_util_avg, kv_cache_miss_rate. Make sure the runner emits stable metric names so dashboards don't break.
ana: ana: I'll draft a small PR to the CI job to toggle auto_shard for the sweep and patch the harness to drop first 60s of telemetry. Will include a flag `--warmup-seconds`.
david: When you open the PR, please also add a test that simulates a worker detach to ensure the rebalancer doesn't run in nightly mode. We can add a synthetic event in the harness that mimics a worker OOM for coverage.
priya: Reproducing locally: run with `--concurrency 48 --token-limit 2000 --duration 120` and watch for `shard_rebalance` logs — usually reproduces in ~3 runs.
matt: If we still see spikes after disabling auto_shard, we should instrument the compilation/kernels selection (we suspect a kernel fallback under long sequences). Add tracepoint when kernel selection falls back to slow path.
priya: Will add tracepoint. For dashboarding: I suggest a per-run tag `sweep-nightly-v2` and a unique run_id so we can correlate regressions with model version/quant profile.
david: Also compute cost-per-token in postprocess: token_cost = (gpu_seconds * gpu_hourly_cost) / tokens_generated. Add that to the report JSON.
priya: I'll include cost-per-token and gpu_util to the JSON. Sample postprocess snippet we can add to harness:
```
# report.json expected fields: run_id, model, quant_profile, tokens_generated, gpu_seconds, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, gpu_util_avg, kv_cache_miss_rate, cost_per_token
```
ci-bot: CI job updated: nightly/sweep now runs with `--warmup-seconds 60` and `--auto-shard=false` for the next 3 runs.
priya: Great. I'll monitor tonight and open PR with tracepoints + cost calc. Thanks all :thumbsup:
matt: If it still flakes, we should add a small canary that runs the same sweep on a dedicated GPU to separate infra noise from runner logic.
priya: noted. Will spin a dedicated GPU canary if needed.
nana: ana: tagging @david for the dashboard schema change.
priya: last note — let's keep the definition of p95 consistent: system-wide p95 over tokens, not per-request p95. That was the other confusion last week.
david: Yup. Add metric name `system.p95_ms` to avoid ambiguity.
priya: thanks, closing the loop for now.
